title: Combustion

match.reason: The bank point covers only complete combustion and the reaction-type classification, with no mention of incomplete combustion producing carbon monoxide or soot, so adding that idea is a new teaching step rather than a small adaptation.

draft.title: Combustion
card: Combustion is a fuel reacting with oxygen and releasing energy as heat and light.
happens with plenty of oxygen. A hydrocarbon gives carbon dioxide and water only.
happens when oxygen is limited. It makes water and also carbon monoxide (CO) or soot (carbon, C), often with some carbon dioxide.
Incomplete combustion releases less energy than complete combustion of the same fuel. A yellow, smoky flame suggests soot, and carbon monoxide is a toxic gas.
draft.remember: Plenty of oxygen gives CO2 and H2O. Limited oxygen can also give CO or soot.

a.q: A gas heater in a small, poorly ventilated room burns methane. Which products suggest incomplete combustion?
opts: Carbon monoxide and water
Carbon dioxide and water
Carbon dioxide and hydrogen
Oxygen and water
a.why: Carbon monoxide forms when oxygen is limited, so it signals incomplete combustion. Carbon dioxide and water are the products of complete combustion, which is the tempting wrong choice.

b.q: Liam's camp stove burns butane with a bright yellow flame and leaves black marks on the pot. What is the best explanation?
opts: Oxygen is limited, so soot forms
Oxygen is plentiful, so soot forms
Combustion is complete, so carbon forms
The stove releases more energy than it should
b.why: Black marks are soot, which is carbon from incomplete combustion, caused by limited oxygen. Complete combustion gives only carbon dioxide and water. Incomplete combustion releases less energy, not more.
b.clue: Soot is one product of burning with too little oxygen.

b.best: Oxygen is limited, so soot forms

problems.detail: The clue 'Soot is one product of burning with too little oxygen' nearly restates the right option 'Oxygen is limited, so soot forms', so a student can match the clue to the option without linking the yellow flame and black marks to soot.

check.summary: The card and both questions are accurate, and each question has one right answer. The only issue is that the clue for question b nearly gives the answer away, so it should hint at what the black marks are instead.
